claims.text: In situ high-resolution TEM equipped with a heating stage can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at atomic resolution.
Heating will reveal atomic-scale rearrangements in nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The observed rearrangements will be consistent with predicted thermodynamic contributions to enhanced thermal stability.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Incremental heating in an in situ TEM will induce atomic-scale rearrangements and morphological changes in the nanoparticles.
Possible heating-induced changes include surface restructuring or clustering.
Thermal energy induces atomic diffusion and rearrangement in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Atomic diffusion and rearrangement drive the nanoparticle toward a lower-free-energy configuration.
Movement toward a lower-free-energy configuration constitutes evidence of thermodynamically enhanced stability.
Heating may produce observable phase-boundary shifts, surface reconstructions, or clustering.
The observable atomic-scale modifications will align with predicted thermodynamic stabilization effects.
The room-temperature baseline will show uniform elemental distribution and initial structural features before heating.
Particle size and compositional fluctuations may affect the nanoparticles' dynamic response to thermal exposure.
